articles.text:
VINCUE Raises $93 Million To Expand Its AI-First Automotive Retail Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:30 AM
VINCUE Raises $93 Million To Expand Its AI-First Automotive Retail Platform
VINCUE has raised $93 million in growth capital to accelerate development and adoption of its artificial intelligence platform for automotive dealerships.
Wavecrest Growth Partners led the investment, with participation from existing investor FM Capital. VINCUE plans to use the funding to advance its product roadmap and significantly expand its go-to-market, dealer performance, and customer-support organizations.
The investment follows two consecutive years in which VINCUE said it achieved growth of nearly 100%. The company attributed that expansion partly to its vehicle acquisition and merchandising products as franchised dealerships increasingly emphasize used vehicles as an important source of profitability.
VINCUE was founded by Chris Hoke, Danny Zaslavsky, Brian Kellogg, and Jeff Rice as a mobile vehicle-appraisal application. It has since developed a broader platform covering the vehicle lifecycle from inventory planning and acquisition through pricing, management, merchandising, and sale.
Protos Rebuilds VINCUE Around AI
A central focus of the financing is Protos, VINCUE’s new AI-native technology foundation.
Rather than adding AI as a separate feature to an existing platform, VINCUE has rebuilt its technology with AI embedded in the underlying system. The company introduced Protos Intelligence to more than 550 dealers, partners, and automotive professionals at its sold-out UNLEASHED 2026 conference in Kansas City.
Dealers can type or speak questions about their inventory and receive responses in plain language. This is intended to make operational data more accessible while helping dealership employees make faster inventory decisions.
Protos includes Signal Appraisal, which predicts a vehicle’s potential retail sale price. The model recalculates the appraisal as managers adjust gross-profit and inventory-turn objectives, while accounting for the costs associated with holding a vehicle.
Another product, the Predictive Market Report, forecasts wholesale values instead of relying exclusively on historical auction results.
VINCUE also disclosed early performance information from the first 100 dealerships using Buy Center Pro for Service Lane Acquisition. During the first nine months of 2026, those dealers generated an additional $5 million in front-end gross profit from service-lane acquisitions, according to the company.
Buy Center Pro includes an AI agent called Benjamin. VINCUE has also announced more than 20 partner integrations involving companies such as Tekion, DriveCentric, LumaScanner, AppraisalPRO, and Auto Hauler Exchange.
Wavecrest Executives Join The Board
As part of the financing, Wavecrest Managing Partner Deepak Sindwani and Principal Anthony Giannobile joined VINCUE’s board of directors.
They will advise the leadership team on strategy, operating scale, and potential partnerships involving other companies in Wavecrest’s portfolio.
FM Capital also increased its investment in VINCUE. The transportation-focused venture firm typically backs early- and growth-stage companies and draws its investor base from automotive dealers, manufacturers, suppliers, distributors, and insurers.

Promise Robotics Raises CAN$40M in Series B Funding to Expand Automated Homebuilding Network
By Greg Bock · 18 November 2026 · 2 min read
Insider Brief
Promise Robotics has raised CAN$40 million in Series B funding to expand its network of automated homebuilding production facilities across North America.
Led by White Star Capital, with participation from Horizons Ventures, Radical Ventures and PSP Investments, the funding will support expansion of the company’s Factory-as-a-Service platform.
Promise Robotics has a multi-year agreement with D.R. Horton, operates production facilities in Canada and has more than 2,500 housing units under contract across three markets.
Promise Robotics has raised CAN$40 million in Series B funding to expand its network of automated production facilities for homebuilders across North America.
White Star Capital led the round, with participation from Horizons Ventures , Radical Ventures and Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments), according to the company . The funding will go to expanding its production network, allowing more builders to access robotic manufacturing without developing and operating their own factories.
Promise’s Factory-as-a-Service platform takes existing home designs and converts them into a coordinated process covering robotic manufacturing, factory operations and installation at construction sites. The company said the system is designed to shorten construction schedules and increase production capacity while reducing builders’ dependence on skilled construction labor.
“Homebuilding can’t scale on trade labor alone, and builders shouldn’t have to become manufacturers to grow. We’re building the production infrastructure the industry can scale on; a network of intelligent factories that get better with every home it helps build,” said co-founder and CEO Ramtin Attar. “This round lets us extend that network across North America.”
The announcement follows a multi-year commercial agreement with D.R. Horton , the largest U.S. homebuilder by volume. According to Promise Robotics, D.R. Horton is the first major U.S. homebuilder to adopt its Factory-as-a-Service platform.
Promise Robotics, which has spent six years developing its technology and business model, operates production facilities in Calgary and Nisku, Canada, and plans to open its first U.S. facility in Phoenix, Arizona. The company reported more than 2,500 housing units under contract across three markets.

The latest investment takes Olyv’s total Series B funding to ~$30 million.

Bengaluru, November 18th, 2026: Olyv, a fast-growing credit-led fintech platform focused on Emerging India, has raised ~$6 million (~₹57 crore) from Nippon Life India AIF Management Limited (hereinafter referred to as “Nippon India Alternative Investments”) along with existing investors, extending the total Series B funding round to ~$30 million. With this investment, Nippon India Alternative Investments joins Olyv’s roster of marquee institutional investors, alongside existing investors Fundamentum and SMBC Asia Rising Fund, adding the strength of a leading global investment institution to its investor base.
The addition brings the backing of a leading global investment institution to Olyv’s investor base, further strengthening its institutional support as the company continues to scale its business and expand its offerings.
Olyv was founded in 2016 by Rohit Garg, Amit Chandel, Vinay Singh, and Jayant Upadhyay, and today offers products across Personal Loans, Gold Savings, and Credit Health management. With nearly 2 million monthly active users and over 5 crore app downloads, Olyv serves customers across 19,000+ pin codes in India.
To date, Olyv has disbursed ~80 lakh loans and facilitated ~₹13,000 crore in cumulative transactions, while consistently increasing PAT profitability for 14 consecutive quarters. By FY29, the company is targeting a user base of 100 million and AUM of over $1 billion.
Rohit Garg, Co-founder and CEO, Olyv, said, “We are delighted to welcome Nippon India Alternative Investments to Olyv’s investor base. Their participation reflects the confidence that leading global institutions are placing in the opportunity we are building. As we enter our next phase, we are continuing to expand the breadth of our platform, invest in technology and products, and reach the next billion hardworking and underserved consumers with greater financial access and utility.”
With Nippon India Alternative Investments joining its investor base, Olyv is further strengthening a shareholder ecosystem that includes global and Indian fintech-focused investors. Since inception, the company has raised ~50 million in equity and ~150 million in debt, with investors including Fundamentum, SMBC Asia Rising Fund, Lightrock, Unicorn India Ventures, India SME, as well as reputed family offices, including Gauri Khan’s Family Office, and prominent entrepreneurs and sports personalities.
About Olyv:
Co-founded in 2016 by Rohit Garg (IIM-A & IIT-K), Amit Chandel (IIT-B), Vinay Singh (IIT-B), and Jayant Upadhyay (IIT-D), Olyv started as an app-based digital lending platform, tied up with RBI-registered lenders to provide quick personal loans to the underbanked self-employed and salaried individuals of India. articles.snippet:

The post O15 Capital Supports 11th St. Workshop Acquisition With $23.6 Million Facility appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
O15 Capital Supports 11th St. Workshop Acquisition With $23.6 Million Facility
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:26 PM
O15 Capital Supports 11th St. Workshop Acquisition With $23.6 Million Facility
O15 Capital Partners has provided debt and equity financing supporting Bluestone Equity Partners’ acquisition of 11th St. Workshop.
Through its Emerging America Credit Opportunities fund, O15 supplied a senior secured last-out term loan as part of a $23.6 million unitranche facility. The firm also made an equity co-investment.
The transaction provides additional detail about the financing behind Bluestone’s acquisition of a majority stake in 11th St. Workshop, which designs and fabricates physical environments for brand activations, events, and other experiential projects.
Flexible Capital For A Lower-Middle-Market Acquisition
A unitranche facility combines senior and subordinated debt into a single financing structure for the borrower. Within that arrangement, a last-out lender generally agrees to receive repayment after first-out lenders under the terms of an intercreditor agreement.
This structure can simplify a company’s debt package while allowing different capital providers to assume distinct levels of risk.
O15’s equity co-investment also gives the firm ownership exposure alongside its credit position.
The investment reflects O15’s strategy of partnering with established private equity sponsors and providing flexible capital to lower-middle-market businesses.
Financial terms beyond the $23.6 million facility were not disclosed.
Supporting 11th Street’s National Expansion
11th St. Workshop works with agencies and brands to design, manufacture, and install complex physical environments.
Bluestone plans to invest in additional production capacity and services while expanding the company’s presence in sports, entertainment, and experiential marketing.
11th Street has begun increasing capacity at its Los Angeles facility and intends to build a broader national platform.
The financing from O15 will support the acquisition and provide a capital structure for that next growth phase.
Bluestone specializes in sports, media, and entertainment investments. O15 focuses on growth capital for lower-middle-market businesses and underserved communities across healthcare, education, and business services.
The parties did not disclose the unitranche facility’s interest rate, maturity date, repayment schedule, leverage ratio, or the size of O15’s equity co-investment.
KEY QUOTES:
11th St. Workshop has built a differentiated platform at the intersection of creative design and highly specialized physical execution, supported by a blue-chip customer base and a reputation for delivering complex, high-profile activations. We’re excited to partner with the Bluestone and 11th St. Workshop teams as the Company builds a leading national platform.
Harry Savage, Principal at O15 Capital Partners
Experiential marketing is one of the fastest-growing areas of advertising spend, and 11th St. Workshop is a trusted partner for agencies and brands on their most high-profile builds. The o15 team delivered a flexible financing package to support our acquisition, and we look forward to partnering with them to enable the Company’s long-term growth.
Shaaz Khan, Senior Vice President at Bluestone Equity Partners

SEATTLE , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- StepSecurity , the cybersecurity company that prevents supply chain attacks, today announced an oversubscribed $20 million round of Series A funding. In combination with a previous seed funding round of $3 million, this brings the total of funding raised to date to $23 million. The round was led by Elephant, with participation from existing investors Runtime Ventures, Inner Loop Capital, and SaaS Ventures. With this funding, StepSecurity will accelerate the development and distribution of its comprehensive platform, which combines developer-machine protection, repository checks, Secure Registry, and Harden-Runner for CI/CD to block malicious packages at all control points in the agentic software pipeline.
Continue Reading
StepSecurity Co-founders Ashish Kurmi and Varun Sharma
"We founded StepSecurity in 2021 because we wanted security teams to have visibility and protection in the environments where software gets built," said Varun Sharma, Co-founder and CEO, StepSecurity. "With this Series A funding, we enter our next phase of growth with years of experience protecting development environments, a solid foundation of trust earned through open-source expertise, and a host of advanced products shaped by real supply chain attacks."
Recent software supply chain attacks have increasingly weaponized malicious packages, automated installation hooks, and hijacked developer accounts to target popular ecosystems like npm, IDE extensions, and AI agents. The need to secure development environments has never been more urgent, as illustrated by recent high-profile security breaches:
The $6.3 Billion Breach at Binance (October 2026): A threat actor, whom the FBI has identified as North Korea's TraderTraitor group, compromised a developer's laptop to access an internal service container with the permissions to initiate withdrawal requests. Using that access as a starting point, the attackers exploited additional points of compromise and an Ethereum account-delegation mechanism to gain transaction approval authority over a hot wallet . In around 20 minutes, the threat actors drained billions of dollars in assets.
Claude Code Extension Tampering (October 2026): A tampered copy of the Claude Code extension was served on the Cursor Extension Marketplace for several hours to deploy a persistent SSH backdoor.
The Shai-Hulud Attack Series (2025-2026 ) : Attackers hijacked developer credentials and pushed hundreds of malicious packages via a major, self-replicating software supply chain worm and cyberattack campaign targeting the open-source npm and PyPI ecosystems.
The StepSecurity platform combines developer-machine protection, repository checks, Secure Registry, and Harden-Runner for CI/CD. With StepSecurity, a malicious component that gets past one layer will still be detected or blocked at another. "We believe independent controls at all control points in agentic software pipelines are the strongest defense for agentic software development," explained Ashish Kurmi, Co-founder and CTO, StepSecurity.
